claims.claim: You can apply or do this online.
claims.note: The text says IHT400 is downloaded, can be filled in on screen and printed, and is sent to the address on the form; it never says the return can be submitted online.

claims.claim: You can apply or do this by post.
claims.quote: You need to download and complete form IHT400 . Send it to the address on the form.
claims.note: The completed IHT400 is sent to the address on the form.

claims.claim: IHT400 applies to the estate of a deceased person.
claims.quote: You must report the full details of the estate and its value to HM Revenue and Customs ( HMRC ) by completing form IHT400.
claims.note: IHT400 reports the estate of someone who has died.

claims.claim: It applies to estates in England and Wales.
claims.quote: You’ll need this code to apply for probate in England and Wales or confirmation in Scotland.
claims.note: The code HMRC sends after IHT400 is used for probate in England and Wales; the text says it also applies in Scotland.

claims.claim: It applies to estates in Northern Ireland.
claims.quote: If you’re applying for probate in Northern Ireland Complete form IHT421 and send it to HMRC with form IHT400 .
claims.note: Northern Ireland applicants send IHT400 with form IHT421.

claims.claim: The IHT400 form must be completed.
claims.quote: Report the value of the estate by completing form IHT400 You need to download and complete form IHT400 .
claims.note: The IHT400 form itself is required.

claims.claim: Relevant supplementary schedules must be completed and sent.
claims.quote: complete and send any relevant additional pages (known as ‘schedules’)
claims.note: Relevant schedules must be sent with the form.

claims.claim: Valuations of all assets are needed.
claims.quote: You’ll need to give accurate valuations when you complete the form.
claims.note: Accurate valuations are required, and full details are defined as the estate's assets and debts.

claims.claim: A copy of the will must be sent.
claims.quote: only send a copy of the will (if there is one) and include copies of any official alterations (known as ‘codicils’) - do not send any originals
claims.note: A copy of the will, if there is one, is sent with the form.
